sections.title: Three more expressions
sections.content: You know the subjunctive after value judgments such as *es importante que* from A2 Unit 27, and *conviene que* and *es mejor que* from B2 Unit 4. You also know that when the subject does not change, Spanish prefers the infinitive (B2 Unit 4). Three more expressions work in the same way: *hace falta que* "it is necessary that", *basta con que* "it is enough that" and *urge que* "it is urgent that". They are all followed by the subjunctive when there is a new subject.

sections.title: Subjunctive or infinitive
rows: We need to arrive early. (new subject: subjunctive)
Arriving early is necessary. (no new subject: infinitive)
It is enough that you call. (subjunctive)
It is urgent that they fix it. (subjunctive)

items.spanish: Hace falta que cada uno traiga algo de comer.
items.english: Everyone needs to bring something to eat.

items.spanish: Basta con que nos avises un día antes.
items.english: It is enough that you let us know a day before.

items.spanish: Urge que arreglen la puerta de la oficina.
items.english: It is urgent that they fix the office door.

sections.content: *Hacer falta* also works with a noun: *Hace falta tiempo*, *Hacen falta más sillas*. The verb agrees with the noun, as it does with *gustar*. With *que* it stays singular: *Hace falta que…*. Do not use the indicative after these three expressions, even when the thing is real: you are judging it, not announcing it.
